transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alejandra Ruiz (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Nina Carter (Lumina Head of AI), Marcus Lee (Lumina Platform Eng), Priya Singh (Lumina Security), Evan Cho (Lumina ML Eng), Jade Kim (Lumina Product)

Summary: Quick intro, alignment on what "POC success" means, then deep into harness integration and what scripts/data Lumina will provide. Discuss tradeoffs streaming vs non-streaming, warmup, KV cache priming, and quantization/accuracy checks.

[00:00] Alejandra: Hey everyone thanks for joining, just to confirm agenda we'll do intros then scoping for the benchmark harness integration, and walk through what we'll need from Lumina for representative traffic.
[00:15] Nina: yep thanks Alejandra, excited. Our main goal is to validate latency and cost numbers for a patient-facing summarization endpoint. We want p95 under 300ms for short summaries (~250 tokens) and stable throughput to support 50 rps.
[00:30] Samir: okay great, couple clarifying q's: is the 250 token estimate inclusive of system + user tokens? also is 50 rps steady or bursty?
[00:45] Nina: 250 tokens per response on average, system + user included. Traffic is spiky, baseline 20 rps with bursts to 60 for 30s every few minutes.
[01:05] Marcus: also we have 3 regions, but for the POC we can focus on east-us region first. we run in our VPC and want to measure both hosted (redwood-hosted) and a private deployment in a later phase.
[01:25] Priya: security note - we need SOC2 artifacts, KMS key handling, audit logs, and SSO/SAML integration details before we run any production-like test.
[01:40] Alejandra: totally, we'll share SOC2 docs and KMS integration notes. For the harness: we have an open repo with runner, load generator harness (python/Go), and sample scripts. Samir will share baseline configs.
[02:00] Samir: the harness supports two modes: non-streaming (HTTP request/response) and streaming (websocket/chunked responses). important to test both because streaming changes bandwidth/CPU patterns and latency p95 is measured differently.
[02:20] Evan: question - for streaming tests, do you simulate incremental tokens or full-chunk sends? Our production uses incremental streaming to show partial summary as it generates.
[02:35] Samir: the harness can do either. we have a streaming client that sends an initial request and then records time-to-first-chunk, inter-chunk latencies, and time-to-complete. we'll include scripts to vary chunk sizes and throttle to mimic client-side rendering.
[02:55] Jade: from product perspective we need quality checks too - not just perf. We'll run automated evals on a sample prompt set to compare Rouge/BLEU-ish metrics and human spot checks.
[03:15] Samir: yes we'll run quality evals using the same harness. baseline flow: run functional correctness (unit prompts), then load tests with correctness sampling at intervals (every 1000 requests sample 10 responses).
[03:35] Marcus: what's the recommended warmup for KV cache / model warm-cache? we've seen first-request p50 be very high until cache warms.
[03:50] Samir: recommend 10-15 minutes at 20% test load to prime KV cache, or run explicit prefix priming script. we'll provide a priming script that replays common prefixes to warm the KV. also the harness has a cache-hit metric. note sometimes transcription shows KV "cash" in our docs, ignore that.
[04:15] Nina: how do you measure cost? we want estimated $/1000 requests based on tokens and GPU-hours.
[04:30] Alejandra: we'll provide per-token and per-hour estimates from the runtime given the chosen quantization and batching config. the harness will report token counts, GPU utilization, and extrapolate cost.
[04:45] Priya: for security we need logs to be delivered to our SIEM and ensure no raw PHI leaves the VPC for private deployment. For hosted run, redwood needs to support token redaction and retention policies.
[05:05] Alejandra: noted. we'll include our retention config and redaction options in the docs. For the initial POC hosted tests we'll use pseudonymized data or synthetic traces.
[05:20] Nina: timeline - we want results within two weeks. internal stakeholders expect a short report and a runbook for integration.
[05:35] Alejandra: realistic timeline: share harness + runbook by tomorrow, Lumina shares traffic script by 3/22, schedule load run for 3/24, analysis rollup 3/26. Is that ok?
[05:55] Marcus: sounds good. also can we run both streaming and non-streaming in the same window or separate? streaming may need different metric collectors.
[06:10] Samir: we can run sequentially in the same window - start with non-streaming baseline, then streaming tests. we'll allocate warmup time between them. the harness will tag runs so metrics don't mix.
[06:30] Evan: slight aside: our current internal endpoint has 180ms median, but 95th is 650ms - so we need to see improvements or comparable cost. we also want to test quantized model variants for cost saving without losing quality.
[06:50] Samir: the harness will support testing model variants and quantization levels. we'll include instructions on how to pin model versions and how rollback works. we'll also add a step to test a float16 vs quantized int8 pipeline.
[07:10] Nina: what about concurrency / batching effects? our traffic is conversational and bursts cause queues. we need to know tradeoffs batch size has on latency vs throughput.
[07:25] Samir: we'll include param sweeps: batch sizes, request timeouts, and target concurrency. the harness supports synthetic bursts to match your 30s spikes. metrics we'll capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, queue depth, and batch composition.
[07:50] Jade: on reporting, can you provide per-route dashboards and a short slide deck summarizing cost/latency/quality tradeoffs?
[07:59] Alejandra: yes we'll provide dashboard exports and a concise deck with recommendations.
[08:10] Priya: one more security question: for hosted tests can we require that logs excluding payload are forwarded to our SIEM and request-level payloads are only seen by RW for the duration of the test (then deleted)?
[08:28] Alejandra: we can sign an NDA if needed; procedurally we support redaction and limited retention. we'll capture that in the security doc Samir will send.
[08:45] Marcus: about instrumentation - does the harness push metrics to Prometheus/Grafana or do you provide CSVs?
[08:58] Samir: both. the harness can push metrics to a prometheus endpoint, or export time-series CSVs. we'll provide a Grafana dashboard template.
[09:12] Nina: ok let's lock success criteria: p95 under 300ms for 250-token summary at 50 rps steady; end-to-end cost target <= $X per 1k requests (we'll decide dollar target after you send initial cost calc); quality: automated eval score drop <= 3% compared to baseline.
[09:35] Alejandra: noted, we'll run to those targets and report back.
[09:44] Evan: small note - our client uses streaming to display partials, so time-to-first-chunk target is important - ideally <100ms.
[09:55] Samir: we'll measure time-to-first-chunk and first-byte latency. streaming also affects CPU and network usage differently vs non-streaming.
[10:10] Jade: can we include synthetic errors to test graceful degradation and fallbacks? for example failing over to a smaller model if latency exceeds threshold.
[10:22] Samir: yes harness includes failure injection (500s, timeouts) and we can simulate automatic fallback to a lower-cost model. we'll capture failover latency and error rates.
[10:40] Nina: ok last piece: data for tests. we'll provide a sanitized set and a traffic generator that replays request timestamps and payload sizes. Marcus will coordinate.
[10:52] Marcus: I'll upload the sample script and 7 days of anonymized traces to the shared folder by 3/22.
[11:05] Alejandra: recap next steps: share harness + runbook, Lumina share traffic traces, schedule 3/24 test window, Samir baseline configs. We'll follow up with a calendar invite.
[11:20] Priya: will review security docs; may ask a few clarifying questions but overall looks good.
[11:30] Alejandra: great thanks everyone, we'll close and follow up via email with links.

Notes on transcript quality: Auto-transcript had a few mis-heard terms (KV cash -> KV cache), speaker labels were mostly accurate. Intent: keep the raw feel, don't over-clean.

End of call.
